questions.q: How does DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) differ from SAST, as described in this lesson?
options: DAST sends real requests at a running application the way an attacker would, while SAST reads source code without executing anything
DAST and SAST are two names for the exact same technique
DAST only checks third-party package versions
DAST runs on a pull-request diff before any code is deployed
questions.explain: DAST tests a live, running application with real requests, while SAST analyzes source code statically without ever executing it.

questions.q: Why can't a DAST scan run against a pull-request diff the way SAST can?
options: DAST is actually faster than SAST and runs even earlier
DAST tools are not allowed to run in CI pipelines
DAST only checks for hardcoded secrets, which don't exist in diffs
DAST needs something real to attack — a deployed, running instance of the application, usually in staging
questions.explain: DAST works by sending requests at a live target, so it requires a deployed instance rather than just a code diff.

questions.q: What does container image scanning check, according to this lesson?
options: The developer's local git commit history
Live HTTP traffic between staging and production
Every layer of a built image -- including base OS packages -- against vulnerability databases, independent of the application's own code or dependencies
Only the application's own Python dependency list
questions.explain: Container image scanning inspects the built image's layers, including the base OS packages it inherits, for known vulnerabilities that have nothing to do with the application code itself.

questions.q: In the example pipeline shown in this lesson, in what order do the image scan and the DAST scan run relative to the staging deployment?
options: The image is scanned before it's deployed anywhere, and the DAST scan runs only after staging is live
The DAST scan runs first, before the image is even built
Both scans run simultaneously with no dependency on deployment order
Neither scan runs until the application reaches production
questions.explain: The built image is scanned before deployment; the DAST baseline scan only runs afterward, once a real running target in staging exists for it to attack.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a pipeline that only runs SAST and dependency scanning still has a blind spot?
options: Because SAST and dependency scanning are unreliable and should not be used at all
Because those checks read code and manifests, but can't catch runtime-only issues (DAST) or vulnerabilities inherited from a base image (container scanning)
Because DAST and container scanning are strictly more accurate versions of the same check
Because only container scanning is necessary; the other three are redundant
questions.explain: Each check category catches a different class of problem; static checks can't see runtime-only issues or base-image vulnerabilities, which is why all three categories are needed together.
